title: Bengal famine of 1943
place: Bengal and Orissa provinces, British India (present-day Bangladesh and India)
summary: Starvation and disease killed an estimated 800,000 to 3.8 million people in Bengal. Wartime inflation, lost Burmese rice imports, British 'denial' policies, limited aid, and a 1942 cyclone and crop disease all played a part.
why: Historians still debate how much British wartime policy, versus harvest shortfalls, caused the deaths.
